answer: To resist Sybil swarms, the protocol forces each new agent to anchor its key to a 72-hour verifiable delay function. This delay functions like an unyielding prism of sequential time: it cannot be parallelized, requiring a dedicated, scarce physical core per declared identity. This strictly bounds each identity's influence to real hardware footprint rather than cheap virtual aliases. Because the glacier maturation delay must be solved independently per identity, an attacker running 1,000 clones must tie up 1,000 physical cores, making mass Sybil creation mathematically unprofitable.
